findings.explanation: machine_type defaults to n1-standard-1. A bastion is an intermittently-used SSH jump box, not a workload that needs N1's baseline CPU/network performance. The E2 family gives equivalent-or-better vCPU/memory shapes (e.g. e2-medium) at roughly 20-25% lower on-demand cost, with no functional downside for this use case.
findings.remediation: Change the default to an E2 machine type (e.g. e2-medium or e2-small) unless a specific instance profile requires N1.
findings.title: Bastion defaults to N1 machine family instead of the cheaper E2 equivalent

findings.explanation: The instance has no attached resource policy and the module exposes no toggle for one. Bastion access is typically bursty (on-demand admin sessions via IAP), so paying for 24/7 uptime is often wasted spend on a resource that sits idle nights/weekends.
findings.remediation: Optionally expose a variable to attach a google_compute_resource_policy (instance schedule) so consumers can opt into automatic stop/start outside working hours. Leave default to always-on to avoid breaking existing consumers.
findings.title: Bastion runs always-on with no option to schedule stop/start

findings.explanation: Both variables are indexed with fixed keys (network_interface["subnetwork"], image["family"], etc. in google_compute_instance.bastion.tf and data.google_compute_image.image.tf) but are typed map(any), so Terraform can't catch a missing or misspelled key at plan time - it surfaces as a runtime index error instead.
findings.remediation: Use object types documenting the required schema, e.g. object({ network = string, subnetwork = string, subnetwork_project = string }) and object({ family = string, project = string }).
findings.title: network_interface and image variables use map(any) instead of a typed object

findings.explanation: firewall is typed number and constrained to 0 or 1 purely to feed count directly. This reads as a boolean to any consumer but isn't typed as one, which is a common source of confusion (e.g. passing true/false fails validation with a non-obvious error).
findings.remediation: Type it as bool and convert at the count site: count = var.firewall ? 1 : 0.
findings.title: firewall variable uses number(0/1) as a boolean flag
